author: Aurelius
quote: My name is Aurelius, but that name will not survive the ages. I am - no, was - a member of the Inquisition, the great and holy secret police of the vast and powerful Zarosian Empire.

author: Aurelius
quote: It was our duty to walk the Empire in secret and to uncover and remove heretics and blasphemers, for our world was poisoned by them.

author: Aurelius
quote: The betrayal began with a whisper. Rumours are like viruses, passing their infection on to more and more people as they go. We did not know where the rumour began, but we knew what it was saying, it whispered 'Zaros has left us, Zaros has gone'. It is true that our deity had not been seen in some time, but to think we had been abandoned was such blasphemy, we could not permit that rumour to be spread further. Kolton and I were tasked with investigating the rumour, to seek out where it had originated and resolve the problem, preferably permanently.

author: Aurelius
quote: As was our system, Kolton donned his finery and waded into the crowd to carouse and converse, whereas I used the statues. The statues are our eyes across the city, they belong to the Inquisition, even the Praetorians do not know how to use them properly. In solace and silence I fed the statues the offerings of sacred shadows and I slipped into the sacred realm of Zaros. [...] We are unseen in this realm [...] We hear in hushed tones and whispers, but we can hear each word that is said.

author: Aurelius
quote: As Kolton placed bets and made friends, I listened to the crowd. [...] I heard tiny blasphemies throughout, enough to put their names in my book, but no greater heresy.

author: Aurelius
quote: For though my investigation had proved fruitless, though the rumours seemed to be the whispers of only a handful of nobodies, they had found their way into my thoughts and I could not shake them. The truth was I had not seen our god for quite some time. [...] We never said anything of it of course, but I know Kolton was afflicted as was I.

author: Aurelius
quote: We were not alone in our doubt. It was clear that a malaise had fallen across the Inquisition. Even the ever-implacable Kharshai seemed to have lost some of the sturdiness in his stance. The Inquisition Office was unusually quiet over the next few days.

author: Aurelius
quote: Once completed I found myself staring at the file of one of our latest detainees, my old partner Cassius. He was changed from the fiery soldier of the church that I once knew. He was broken, partially because of the torture we'd put him through, but mostly in spirit. [...] 'We are alone.' He kept whispering. 'He isn't there.' [...] I tried to change his heart by reasoning that the Empire was functioning to perfection, so Zaros's guiding hand must be present, but he was unmoved.

author: Aurelius
quote: In desperation, I asked him how he knew this. His answer chilled me. 'The Shadow tells me so.'

author: Aurelius
quote: I asked Cassius what this Shadow was and he looked at me with a half smile that sent shivers down my spine. 'Don't you hear it whispering?' he said. 'The statues must hear it. They must. Because it is through them that the Shadow speaks.'

author: Aurelius
quote: Nonsense rambling. Madness. A pity, he had been a good man and a good friend. I took no joy in his execution.

author: Aurelius
quote: I spent some time in the Shadow Realm, walking the paths the statues showed us. I strained my ears for signs of this whispering nonsense, this 'Shadow' that Cassius had raved about even in his death throes. But there was nothing. [...] More and more I became convinced that the rumours were the nonsense chatterings of a broken mind.

author: Aurelius
quote: But then I reached the bridge. [...] on that day, I heard her, and it's never seemed quite the same since. Her voice was barely more than a whisper, but it was there. She sounded like my daughter, who had died from sickness a few years prior. But strangely she also sounded like my wife, my mother and my grandmother, all of whom had passed on. They whispered in one shared voice and I could not help but listen.

author: Aurelius
quote: They told me to be vigilant. That Zaros was gone, but he had not abandoned us. But in his absence forces were moving to take his place. To seize power and to destroy us from within. They reminded me that we were not the only secret police and that a city doesn't need two secret organisations. I had to learn what the Praetorians were doing.

author: Aurelius
quote: I had informed Kolton of the whispering and brought him to the bridge to discover them himself. [...] then we both heard the voice. [...] The whispering voice warned us of absent gods and all to present betrayals. It described in vague prophecy the promises of the Praetorians' crimes. As we listened, it told us of dark and sinister experiments beneath the city. The Praetorians were trying to uncover something old, something buried and something dangerous. Something that would threaten even Zaros himself. The ultimate blasphemy.

author: Aurelius
quote: Kolton and I agreed they had to be stopped, but we needed proof. We had to find a way to observe them, and there was only one option.

author: Aurelius
quote: We followed Sliske for some time, though Kolton refused to believe that his friend could possibly have anything to do with the heresy the whispering promised us.

author: Aurelius
quote: We followed him across the city, through the market, past the Colosseum and the Wards, finally coming to stop inside the Grand Cathedral's grounds. [...] After a few minutes, he stood and walked over to one of the statues. With horror, I saw him take out the catalyst that would propel him into the same hidden realm as us. [...] In desperation, we ducked down behind the very pew Sliske had been praying in. [...] When we emerged, Sliske had vanished, but there was a strange heaviness in the air.

author: Aurelius
quote: I looked closely at the statue he had been using and I felt a strange chill, as if the Shadow Realm were thicker there. Had Sliske found a way to journey deeper into this transcendant plane?

author: Aurelius
quote: It took all the magic at our disposal to bring us deeper into the Shadow Realm, deeper than I had ever been.

author: Aurelius
quote: 'It's an old motto,' he said. 'Sliske and I would psyche ourselves up for a battle by repeating those words as a mantra. It makes sense that he would use them as part of all this.' His expression was as unreadable as the stony features of any Mahjarrat, but I understood the sorrow it must be hiding. Sliske was his friend, and this phrase was like a signature on a confession, proving that Sliske was up to something - here, at this most sacred of places.

author: Aurelius
quote: As the mask's face fell away from the statue, we felt a sensation dragging us down. When it had finished, we found ourselves in a room we had never seen, staring into a hole in the Universe.

author: Aurelius
quote: The chamber was dominated by a single structure, a strange monolith hovering in the air. At the centre of the monolith there seemed to be a swirling vortex of some kind and from it came the whispering voice.

author: Aurelius
quote: 'What are you?' I found myself whimpering, desperate to comprehend the incomprehensible. 'Vos,' it said, as though this were a sufficient answer.

author: Aurelius
quote: It promised me everything I wanted: the evidence needed to convict Sliske, the chance to get my family back, everything I'd ever dreamed... if I would only touch the monolith. It was intoxicating. But I am an Inquisitor, and we do not give in to simple temptation. I steeled myself and turned away, and my gaze fell upon Kolton. His eyes were wide in equal parts wonder and horror and I felt the monolith reaching out to him, using the Shadow Realm as arms. In a flash, I saw the last vestige of sanity torn from his mind and he fell into a stupor on the floor, drooling like an animal.

author: Aurelius
quote: As I felt the whispering voice reach out to me, promising me everything, I found myself less and less able to deny it. Its needs were so simple, all I had to do were to touch the monolith and to open that crack in the world just a fraction more. I just had to let more of it in. It was so reasonable. So simple. How could I deny it that when it promised me everything in return? Fortunately, Zaros intervened.

author: Aurelius
quote: The fury of a god is the stuff of legend. [...] Zaros's rage was so perfectly controlled - so locked away - that it became a heavy weight pushing me down. [...] With a snap, the monolith closed tight. It had barely opened - the difference between closed and open was imperceptible. But now that compulsive feeling was gone, and only the rage of a god bore down on me. I knew now that this was a sacred place. A place belonging only to Zaros. A place where he could enact his divine will without interference or distraction. In our blind curiosity, we had trespassed upon this ground.

author: Aurelius
quote: In the days to come, Zaros began to restrain the power and reach of the Inquisition. We were denied the use of the statues and we were far more restricted in our duties. The Praetorians picked up the slack and as we diminished, their flame grew brighter. Each time I saw Sliske, I saw that maddening grin - that jester's smile that belied a cold, cruel and calculating mind. He had destroyed us with a whisper, and I had been such a fool.

author: Aurelius
quote: Poor Kolton never regained control of his mind. It made him the perfect sacrifice for that cruel Mahjarrat ritual. [...] It will not surprise you to learn that I was stripped of my title as Inquisitor.

author: Aurelius
quote: I write these words not for posterity, nor fame, but simply because I have no one left to talk to. My life was one of secrecy and silence and so it is fitting that it should end in the same way. Still, I feel that urge to leave something behind, a small reminder to the world that I existed. So, I write these memoirs of the events that would lead to my end.

author: Aurelius
quote: Now, I find myself now alone and mostly forgotten, as it should be. The only problem is I keep hearing the whispering voice calling to me. Even now as I write this I hear that beautiful song, urging me to find it again. This time, though, there is no god to stop me. Its asks so little and its song is so beautiful.

author: Aurelius
quote: As Kolton placed bets and made friends, I listened to the crowd. I heard the human Marellius utter Zaros's name in vain. [...] I heard tiny blasphemies throughout, enough to put their names in my book, but no greater heresy. There were no whispers of an absent god, nor concerns of abandonment. The crowds seemed content with the world and our investigation turned out to be fruitless.

author: Aurelius
quote: As Kolton placed bets and made friends, I listened to the crowd. [...] I heard the widow Rothbry complain about the vampyres, questioning why such creatures are allowed in a civilised city. I heard tiny blasphemies throughout, enough to put their names in my book, but no greater heresy. There were no whispers of an absent god, nor concerns of abandonment. The crowds seemed content with the world and our investigation turned out to be fruitless.

author: Critic
quote: It is my sad duty to report that theatre is dead, at least if the latest performance of 'A Midwinter Night's Tomfoolery' is to be believed. The play - performed as ever by the Guild Actors of Senntisten - rather live up to the group's acronym, which is to say rather a lot of hot GAS. The leading role of Robinius, the mischievous Chthonian demon who likes to trick people into silly contracts, was performed by the human Aleric White.

author: Critic
quote: There are many good things I can say about the notable acting career of Mr White. Some of his past performances have been the stuff of theatrical legend. Sadly, I can ascribe none of these traits to his current performance. Mr White is not as young as he used to be, and has lost his youthful vigour, charm and good looks. Instead of the sophisticated, eloquent and handsome man of yesteryear, Mr White looks like little more than middle-aged sausagemeat stuffed into tights. His performance has the grace and style of a stone-age ballerina, and his delivery of the text so wooden I was surprised no one attempted to chop him down for firewood.

author: Aurelius
quote: Today there were four suspected heretics that needed my attention. The first was a human called Tobed. He was a strange sort, quiet and gentle, but when he spoke he spoke only blasphemies. He whimpered that there were other gods out there whose designs were more benevolent, or more righteous. Another fool worshipping the pretender god Saradomin simply because his countenance is human. How vain a species we are.

author: Aurelius
quote: Today there were four suspected heretics that needed my attention. [...] The second was Worvim the vampyre. Worvim professed her innocence at each step of interrogation. She had been set up, she claimed, she was faithful, she screamed. We dug as deep as we could, but we uncovered no lies or heresy. Perhaps she was innocent. Only Zaros can judge her now.

author: Aurelius
quote: Today there were four suspected heretics that needed my attention. [...] Zadok was a strange creature who spoke only in gestures and pointless little dances. I could not decipher any true blasphemy from their actions and being irritating is hardly a crime. I let them go.

author: Aurelius
quote: Today there were four suspected heretics that needed my attention. [...] Yokai the necromancer was the final heretic on my list. She was a strange woman, human as far as I could tell, but with a darkness to her.

author: Aurelius
quote: She answered all of my questions with an honesty that was almost charming. She had been digging in the city graveyard again. When I asked her why, she claimed she was seeking out the monstrous creature that was sealed away there. She spoke of the dread corruption that plagued our city so long ago. A monstrous fungus that threatened to consume and infect the city, before it was fought back and sealed away beneath our dead. Nonsense of course.

author: Aurelius
quote: Once completed I found myself staring at the file of one of our latest detainees, my old partner Cassius. He was changed from the fiery soldier of the church that I once knew. He was broken, partially because of the torture we'd put him through, but mostly in spirit. Before me was a portrait of shattered faith. 'We are alone.' He kept whispering. 'He isn't there.' [...] I asked him how he knew this. His answer chilled me. 'The Shadow tells me so.'

author: Aurelius
quote: I tried to change his mind with words from scripture, but they fell on deaf ears. I tried to change his heart by reasoning that the Empire was functioning to perfection, so Zaros's guiding hand must be present, but he was unmoved. His broken spirit could not be beaten back into shape.

author: Aurelius
quote: I asked Cassius what this Shadow was and he looked at me with a half smile that sent shivers down my spine. 'Don't you hear it whispering?' he said. 'The statues must hear it. They must. Because it is through them that the Shadow speaks.' Nonsense rambling. Madness. A pity, he had been a good man and a good friend. I took no joy in his execution.

author: Critic
quote: The leading lady was played by the eminently forgettable Cassandra Stropp. While certainly of a more reasonable age to play Queen Gargantiana - the vampyre queen arguing with her husband over which human to drink [...]

author: Critic
quote: [...] Stropp possesses the emotional range of a cheeseboard with none of the joy. She delivers Gargantiana's lines with the panache of a dead squirrel and her flirtatious moments are so poorly delivered they sound like death threats. Though death would be a merciful end to witnessing this debacle.

author: Critic
quote: Yet another lacklustre performance by the Guild Actors of Senntisten. This time they brutally murdered a rendition of the classic love story 'Cressilius and Troida', the tragic story of a Chthonian demon, madly in love with an Avernic demon. In the role of Troida - the tragic love interest of our Chthonian protagonist - we once again see Cassandra Stropp. Once against she delivers an emotionless performance that make the statues in the town square look like world-class thespians. She delivers each line with a mechanical precision that has no place on the stage.

author: Critic
quote: Yet another lacklustre performance by the Guild Actors of Senntisten. This time they brutally murdered a rendition of the classic love story 'Cressilius and Troida', the tragic story of a Chthonian demon, madly in love with an Avernic demon. [...] The lead role of Cressilius is played for some reason by the youngest of the troupe, Cassius Holter.
name: review2p1

author: Critic
quote: Young Cassius may well be a great actor, but he needs the time to mature and experience in order to grasp the nuance of the chthonian demon's plight. His youthful vigour could perhaps serve him well in the role of a soldier, or some waifish background love interest. But in the role of Cressilius it's practically an insult. Still, the terrible truth is that young Holter is by far the best thing in the play. I'm afraid it's all downhill from there.

author: Critic
quote: It is with great relief that I must announce that the Guild Actors of Senntisten are no more. For anyone that has suffered the torture that is watching any of their plays, I'm sure you will be well aware of the terrible messages underscored in each one. While hidden under a guise of terrible acting, dull deliveries and the costuming skills of a dismembered troll, it appears that the Guild were attempting to weave seditious messages into their work. Evidently, this was done with the same degree of skill as their acting, which is to say none, as these messages were not clearly conveyed to their audience. Still, the Praetorians know what they're doing, and so the Guild Actors of Senntisten must have been performing seditious plays.
name: sedition

name: play2

author: Critic
quote: One can only hope that now that the theatre is mercifully free of the talentless Guild, we can see true talent grace our stage again.

author: Critic
quote: But the strangest of all is the writing. I am used to plays that offer hidden meanings, or play on the emotional states of the viewer. The works of Garenius, which asks the viewer what it really means to be a citizen of the Empire. [...] These plays prey on our own preconceptions and turn our own thoughts into a marvellous piece of the performance. But this play does none of that.

The 'Whispering King' is a [...] play written and directed by none other than the Prefectus Praetorio himself. [...] the strangest of all is the writing. I am used to plays that offer hidden meanings, or play on the emotional states of the viewer. The works of Garenius, which asks the viewer what it really means to be a citizen of the Empire. The wonderful sonnets of Theanopha who urges us to look inside ourselves and understand the secret shames we all keep hidden. These plays prey on our own preconceptions and turn our own thoughts into a marvellous piece of the performance. But this play does none of that. [...] At no point did it make any sense. [...] 2 stars.

author: Critic
quote: I would like to amend my previous review on the 'Whispering King'. I realise now that I was too harsh in my assessment. Indeed, the play is a veritable work of art. I confess that I was blind to the genius hidden therein. [...] I find myself consumed with jealousy for them and their sacrifice. That they could give their lives for the highest purpose. [...] I dream of those last moments as the play concludes and I dream of seeing what they see, of learning what they learn. Of becoming. My mask arrives tomorrow. 5 stars.

Me and Ebony have been dishing it to the Empty Children as best we can, but we've put some of the gold away into the box like you said. I don't know why we ain't spending it though. Another case of a vampyre being torn to shreds in some abandoned house. I've seen three cases like this in as many months. [...] Finally, there's the message by the corpse. It was made in blood, like someone took a finger and dipped it into a wound to write. Four strange words. 'This is for Jelly,' though I have no idea why someone would commit such a brutal act over a dessert.

What appeared on the horizon was a glacor of truly titanic size. [...] As I write this account, I can see the massive glacor moving in the distance. It looms, as tall as a mountain. Storms cling to its side, and a wicked and unholy light shines from within its core. I can see no hope, no survival in this place, but I can still find honour in battle and death. To be the first to slay such a beast. Is it even possible? If this account lies unfinished, you will know that I failed.
author: Fell Arnessen
Fell Arnessen
quote: This was no slow-moving glacier, but an eternal, frozen plain, miles deep. In places the snow was blasted away by the wind, and I could see the murky ice reach down into the depths below where the roots of the mountains lay... As I wandered, I saw shapes through the ice, on the bottom far below. They were too regular or too incredible to be natural rock. They were buildings, great cities even, buried in a frozen, sunken slumber.
name: miles

author: Nex
quote: 'Finally I created the stone of ice from an arch-glacor on the frozen world of Leng. These creatures, that tower ten or a hundred times taller than their smaller kin, dominate the landscape of that brutal and inhospitable wasteland.'

author: Aurelius
quote: She answered all of my questions with an honesty that was almost charming. She had been digging in the city graveyard again. When I asked her why, she claimed she was seeking out the monstrous creature that was sealed away there. She spoke of the dread corruption that plagued our city so long ago. A monstrous fungus that threatened to consume and infect the city, before it was fought back and sealed away beneath our dead. Nonsense of course.

author: Aurelius
quote: To the east I can see the magnificent graveyard. A morbid site, perhaps, but the architecture and the artistry cannot be denied. To the west I see the Grand Cathedral itself, the central structure of the district, gazing out over the city.

author: Sliske
Sliske
quote: I find the comings and goings of demonkind to be quite the bore, but there is something to be said for demonic multiples (twins, triplets, etc). They are, of course, a rare anomaly: a 'difficult birth' from the Heart of Dis that sees a single soul split into multiple physical forms. The separate entities present independent personalities, but they are linked by an unspoken (and unbreakable) pact. They have the ability to communicate over vast distances, and to form unspoken plans in the blink of an eye. They also form a fierce loyalty to one another.

author: Kat (Zamorak's demon invasion)
quote: We all miss you. I know you feel you need to leave on this spiritual journey of self-discovery [...] Mother has been worried about you. [...] I've been hearing whispers and rumours about some sort of terrible evil power growing in the shadows. They say Zamorak is preparing to do something terrible.

author: Lilian
quote: I love being your wife, but being ONLY your wife has never been enough for me. I see the things you are researching - you and your fellow mages. I see the power you wield - the destruction you can cause - and it fills me with a deep envy. Day by day, it poisons my love for you. But there is another way. I have joined a sisterhood of women who crave the power that we deserve.

quote: I am confident that the death of Guthix, which brought about the return of the gods to Gielinor, will loom larger than the comparatively minor events which mark the current Fifth Age. For now, however, I cannot in good conscience formally label it an 'age' when the preceding period would have been a mere 182 years in length.
name: year 182

quote: Your mission is to contact our agent inside Menaphos. Use the tunnels beneath the temple of lesser gods. Be vigilant of traps and the hostile natives. They're about as welcoming as the Menaphites only slightly better looking.
This book - the Umbranomicom, aka the Book of Shadow - details Orcus's revelation that Rasial was a once-human follower of Guthix
This book - the Fumonomicom, aka the Book of Smoke - details how Orcus learned that Rasial used to be a guardian of magic and runes
Though it left me thinking on Misalionar and how sad a final pass. A tragic death with a the murderer who escaped their just fate.
This book - the Sanguinomicom, aka the Book of Blood - details how Orcus tasked the Hereditas Expedition to track down the location of the tomb of Rasial

Aragnya's Veil is dangerous. My kind fear it beyond all else because it disguises what we hold most sacred, that being truth and logic. It was woven because Aragnya was jealous: her legs were not so long as the other females, and she was a cripple. No male would breed with her.
In creating the Veil, she harnessed powers that cannot exist, that defy logic, and with it she spread her unruly genes to generations upon generations of my kind.
The children we ate. As for her, we dared not touch her while she wore the Veil. Instead, we lured her into a place from which she could not escape, and we waited for her to die.
You have told me of your kind, your culture, and I find it wretched. You have slaughtered thousands of innocent children. For that there can be no forgiveness. But there can be justice.

* You toss a single coin into the well.
* 2,147,483,648 coins magically appear in your hands!
* But the coins overflow and fall back down into the well.

author: Nakatra
quote: The Devourer's ritual worked, just like she said it would. The machine is alive. I can sense it. The hum - the same low whirr that hung in the streets of Uzer. But there is something more to it, too. Something in my spirit, pulling me in. Experimentation can begin, but will require a steady supply of sentient sacrifice. I must populate the dungeon.

When the scales of life and death formed the underworld it was but a void, lifeless and devoid of any semblance of our world. Magic flowed unlike the realm of the living, manifesting in four prime elements: Bone, Flesh, Spirit, and Miasma. It was with this magic that the so-called god of balance brought shape to the underworld. With shape came the dead, ferried by the god's chosen vassal. The god, lost in their compassion for the living, failed to foresee that their actions would disturb the flow of true death and the oblivion of the underworld. The elements, once silent, began to gather and pool, disrupted by the young god's actions. Slowly, they twisted, weaved, and grew stronger. It was here that the prime elementals of death were formed. In their antithesis of death, death gave birth to life.
The Lord of Bones was the next to take shape, an emptiness made manifest. It had no want or need, nothing more than a shell of potential. It ventured into the darkness, never to be seen again.

author: Kuthorn Magestis
quote: For Thirty Six years I have been part of the Order of Slayers, spilled blood of monsters, both human and creature. But tonight I fear, the devourer takes me. I've felt a cold upon my neck for a few weeks now, perhaps Death has simply been waiting for the right time. Did I grow complacent in my old age? Or was this always set to be my fate? I suppose it doesn't matter now, death is merely the next step. Soon I will be elsewhere and I will think not of these moments. Embarrassing it did happen at the hands of a Kurask however. Foul beast gave as good as it got. Hopefully I see the sunrise before I go.

author: Kuthorn Magestis
quote: How long has it been? How long have I been here? I need purpose, all I have is questions. The Akh have purpose. The Sanctum is full of them - 'Akh' - Minions of the Devourer. I have heard tales of these creatures before, I believed that they like most monsters to be exaggerations, stories, perhaps hallucinations brought on by desert heat.

author: Kuthorn Magestis
quote: But no, they are very much real. Real but odd, strange creatures. Why do they serve the Devourer? Are they compelled to do her bidding? Ensnared? Is is just their nature? Or like the order is it simply a price to pay? Where do they come from? Are they born of the underworld, or are they living? Blasted. More questions. I lack answers, the more time I spend here, the more the questions manifest. I was hesitant to get close at first, but they pay me no heed, I do not exist to them, they continue ever on with their strange ways. They seem to lack something, It's as if they are empty. Are they soulless?

author: Kuthorn Magestis
quote: Lady Nakatra, she is not like the rest here. She is living. Breathing. How? Why, would a person choose to reside here. Is she cursed?

author: Kuthorn Magestis
quote: She claims some grand purpose, though I could not make head nor tail of it, strange musings of moonstones, souls, the Order and the never-ending whirr? I cannot make sense of any of it. I lack purpose, everything, everyone here seems to have some grand purpose, why not me? Just existence, is that all that remains?

author: Kuthorn Magestis
quote: She keeps secrets close to her chest. My questions met with silence, or riddles at best. 'What am I waiting for?' I ask her. 'Is this it?' 'Soon, the gates will open.' I do not understand. I believe she is losing her mind, this place was not meant for the living, the afterlife is for the dead after all.

It was Number 12 from last month's batch. All materials were standard, construction was standard. [...] But this one was odd, like no golem I've witnessed before... it asked not to be disassembled. Magic is strange and unpredictable. Thankfully, it offered no resistance to the actual process.

Normally, when the light from the window catches a core, the whole room bursts into color; blues and greens scattering in every direction. author: Inaya
quote: One of the core responsibilities of our Order is providing palliative care and preparing the final rites of those nearing the end of their lives. As we ready a soul for their journey to the underworld we light incense and present an offering to each of the three deities of the underworld. A bone for steadfast Icthlarin, that he will guide their soul safely to the underworld. A raw fish for the insatiable Devourer, that she might stay her maw. And a silver coin for the mighty Elidinis, that she will bless them with a painless transition from life to death.

author: Inaya
quote: Many fear this aspect of Elidinis. They yearn for their position in this world to remain stagnant, for their name and deeds to be remembered in perpetuity. Such is their folly. We know that even the strongest stone erodes beneath the water's flow, given time.

author: Inaya
quote: Our lady Elidinis is the matriarch of the Menaphite pantheon, goddess of the moon, who holds domain over fertility, growth, and life, as well as erosion, death, and the Underworld.

My Master believes that The Devourer has poisoned their minds with falsehoods, seeding rumours that he attempted to usurp the pantheon.

Fear, however, does not abate with time. Not when our enemies plot and scheme relentlessly. I have heard tell that the followers of the River Goddess have risen against our kind, and swayed the people of the desert against us. They do not understand my Master's actions, that tunneling beneath Elidinis' river and tapping into her magic was his sole means of sheltering us from The Devourer's clutches. Elidinis' followers went so far as to forge a weapon with the sole purpose of our destruction - the mighty Keris dagger.
The King of Leaves went to live in the Land of Harvest, where it was always autumn.

author: Herbert Dunwich
quote: Where the head should have been instead rose a great many heads, all growing out of a central column which itself was made of more faces, such that there was no neck, only more faces. It unnerved me. What snippets of conversation and prayer I was able to overhear from the creatures regarding this figure gave it a name. I believe this deity is referred to as 'Uvhastur'

author: Aurelius
quote: 'What are you?' I found myself whimpering, desperate to comprehend the incomprehensible. 'Vos,' it said, as though this were a sufficient answer.

author: Skeka
quote: We kin believe in Skekslan, the unbroken wheel - us Aughra doubly so. Kranon has comforted me by reminding me of this, and that Varanus was a standout soul in life, and is revered in death. We may well see his like again. I am not so sure this is true, since I fear the destroyers not only ended our world and our universe, but also that cycle. My personal studies seem to confirm this fear, but it was still a small glimmer of hope for me.
Mother Rimehazel, one of the first witches to join our order.
"What are we but witches?" a question often asked to us when we first join this sacred order.

list: Across the seas, far from the bustling streets of Misthalin and Asgarnia, Rimehazel hailed from a small village of content, narrow-minded individuals.

quote: Such abilities were a test from Saradomin - that one would not walk the 'dark path' - and had no place in the peaceful village's heart.
She was able to feel the very anima that made up this world, able to manipulate it, sense it between her very fingers as you or I might feel a stream of water.
She was smaller than the other children, fish would flee at her very presence, and anything she cooked she would seem to burn.
Rimehazel's powers had almost entirely disappeared by 12, suppressed by the ignorance and short-sightedness of those around her.
They watched as the bandits cut down Rimehazel's father as a warning...and they watched as the bandits walked off into the night, food and gold in tow.
Slowly, Rimehazel's gift trickled back, and as she allowed it to writhe and form, it grew.
Rimehazel didn't hide her abilities any longer, she didn't suppress her powers, and as such she was outcast.
With a outstretched hand she whipped a flame at those who would have taken from her. With twists and turns she smothered the bandits with a cyclone of flames, and when it passed only ashes remained.
Rimehazel, one of the first sisters, brought the entire village to cinders. She did not need the villagers' false praise. Her value - her purpose - was her own..
At our lord's command, we have unleashed the runes. A number of subjects have been taken to the plinth by our lord and Mother Cassia.

Mother Cassia, We have been given new orders. A squadron of my best men are still to lead you to the Undercity to begin preparations.
It is my duty to the empire to report to you illicit occurrences happening in the Undercity under the front of 'Covarz Curios'.
Just this morning I was browsing their wares (attempting to find pieces for my collection, no less).
Kesin, I hope this letter finds you well. It is my duty to the empire to report to you illicit occurrences happening in the Undercity under the front of 'Covarz Curios'.

Smokethistle has shown to have magically reductive properties, and has proven a powerful asset in handling out-of-control magical creatures.
No known specimens have been grown on Gielinor successfully.
Notable for its alluring smell, the pollen of the impshade has strong hallucinogenic effects when inhaled.
While not necessarily a rare plant, it is hard to acquire, as those wishing to gather it often wake up days later, miles from where their excursion started.
As such, demon folk - in particular imps - are frequently used for their gathering as they seem to show an immunity to the plant's intoxicating effects.

In particular, one archer under the banner of the Empire favours arrows dipped in an impshade concoction, allowing the hallucinogenic effects to be administered to the target without the need for an arrow to even hit its target.
However, all reporters misplaced their specimens after involuntarily being afflicted with the impshade pollen.
Demon folklore states the vine was aptly named after the Tsutsroth Vi'Noxiz was found lifeless, having been constricted by a single vine.

Clippings of butcher's binding are often in sedative potions, calming even the most berserk demons. Marksmen have also found use in these mixtures, taking miniscule amounts in order to steady any extraneous bodily movements.
Repeated clippings can be taken from a single plant, if it is appropriately contained.
However, doing so requires the soil to be treated with large amounts of blood, or other animal-based matter.
Identifiable by its ash grey cap, it is commonly mistaken for the poisonous demon's hunch which appears almost identical when covered in the ash and soot of Infernus.

author: The Ambassador
quote: The ritual is prepared... It's beautiful, really, the song. Just notes, sung together in a strange harmony. To think how such a beautiful song could pierce the heavens itself and bring us our salvation.

author: Aurelius
quote: Its words were starlight and dazzled me as it spoke. It promised me everything I wanted: the evidence needed to convict Sliske, the chance to get my family back, everything I'd ever dreamed... [...] Even now as I write this I hear that beautiful song, urging me to find it again. [...] It asks so little and its song is so beautiful.

author: Guthix
quote: Problems so far beyond their capability, that the very land rejected those that lived upon it and their world tried to shed them.

Grarl's Fiery Fiends, the only store stocking rare and curious creatures from across the Empire and beyond! Rats keeping you awake at night? We've got a range of small to large cats that can leave your hovel essentially rat-free. Perhaps you need a fierce companion to intimidate your enemies - we import only the finest hell-canids from across the Infernal lands.

We have been split into research teams, I have been paired with mostly fresh faces although I do recognise the one that was going a bit stir crazy in the Xolo city. I think his name was Matty, I'll keep an eye on him. Could've been him that stole my journal.
The death throes of the rats seem to have shaken the door loose of its hinges. You pick it up and go through.

author: Lowerniel Drakan
quote: The Vitur were in thrall to their long-dead founder, whom they considered a 'god'. He was a figure of awe and wonder to the Vitur, and there were volumes of histories dedicated to him. Indeed, he was not only worshipped by his vyres, but a number of sapient races sacrificed themselves willingly out of respect for him and House Vitur's opulent culture.

author: Lowerniel Drakan
quote: Lord Jovkai was the longest ruling tribal leader in the pre-Zarosian age, and the oldest recorded living vyre. He was a beloved leader, and this love was transposed on to their prey. They would treat their food with care and tenderness, allowing it to live among them feeling safe and cared for...before mercilessly slaughtering it behind closed doors. I was pleasantly surprised by the bloods from this region, a bittersweet taste with a lingering finish.

author: Kaleb

author: Kaleb
quote: Moonrise, the locals call it, though the village elder called it by a different, older name: Akshur-Nakkir.
He led his clan a great distance, to see them released. Chasing tales of those who had fled to the east. On rafts made of logs, the sea they did roam. In search of new land. Their haven. Their home.

His people were different. They struck others with fright. From livestock found slaughtered. From the howling at night. Not wanting a future where their kind were maligned, they said their goodbyes, left the village behind.

They found a small tribe near the mountain's crest, who claimed to precede those who came from the west. In them, kindred spirits. Those also outcast. With the blood of the wolf. Strong ties to the past.

Hawthorn would prove his resolve. He would duel their high priest. In the light of the moon, they began their fight. A contest that raged for two days and three nights. The Great Wolf herself came to watch the display. Coated in blood and sweat, Hawthorn won that day.
With Inanna's blessing, on this site they would dwell. They founded a village, which he named 'Amberfell'.

During the early years of Queen Ninbaradari's reign, however, a series of increasingly severe earthquakes struck the island. The tremors continued for months before culminating in a single catastrophic event. [...] When the dust settled, an enormous circular chasm dominated the landscape, visible for miles in every direction.

Even after the collapse, aftershocks continued to emanate from the newly formed chasm. Intrigued by reports of the phenomenon, Queen Ninbaradari dispatched an expedition from Shuruk-Ba to investigate.

Word of the discovery quickly reached Queen Ninbaradari. Upon witnessing the creature for herself, she immediately abandoned any discussion of mercy. Where others saw a dying god-beast, she saw opportunity. Queen Ninbaradari became convinced that the divine ichor represented the key to ascension itself! Work began almost immediately.

A great ritual was performed within the pit. Through blood magic and divine experimentation, the millipede was prevented from dying. Bound to the mortal plane and incapable of escape, it became a permanent source of divine ichor.

For many years, the harvest appeared successful. Divine ichor was collected in vast quantities. The substance fuelled experiments, strengthened Queen Ninbaradari's followers and became the foundation upon which much of her growing power was built.

By this time, Queen Ninbaradari had largely withdrawn from direct oversight of the harvest. Many blamed her absence for the deterioration, albeit in hushed tones. Others claimed the rituals maintaining the creature had become flawed. New ceremonies were devised. Experiments intensified. Nothing worked.

The Rite of Induction is a sacred ceremony, held on the full moon, marking the formal induction of initiates such as yourself into the great temple of Akshur-Nakkir.

Nakkirian, Lord of Transformation, to show respect for his teachings. Cooked meat for Dilimbabbar, Lord of Cycles, to fuel his strength. And a lit candle for Kayazu, Lord of Ceremonies, to light his path.

Kayazu is oft present to personally bestow his blessing upon his chosen. Dimilbabbar does so on occasion, while Sudumuzid's appearance is a rare sight, and a dark omen. Should your lord be absent their high priest will impart their blessing to you in their stead, as you recite your vows.
You will now have access to the temple interior, and will be guided inside, before emerging wearing the kaunake of the priest. A celebratory feast will be held in your honour.

author: Lowerniel Drakan
quote: The ruler of Alzeph was a contemptible vyre. Those they ate tended to be vyres from other tribes, and the other tribes loathed the Alzeph. Such blood is thankfully rare since the birth of the new aristocracy and the Alzeph now being wiped out. I had the displeasure of tasting some blood from their stores, which was disgustingly spicy and held a grainy texture.

author: Lowerniel Drakan
quote: The Ghrazi were the most vicious of all vampyre tribes, priding themselves on their ability to fight rather than stalk. They would not capture their prey so much as bait it, goad it into combat. They would only hunt the most fearsome and territorial beasts of Vampyrium, not the myriad of docile creatures. They believed they were ingesting the strength of all they ate. Personally, I found the aggression within the blood of such creatures to be foul - swill for an unrefined palate, not fitting for a cultured society. The tribe took to our burgeoning society poorly, with the vast majority being clipped and effectively used as pack animals for our hunts. If not for their ferocity in battle, I'd have had them all put down.

author: Lowerniel Drakan
quote: The Myrmel tribe would stalk entire families or social groups, quickly striking down one of their number, yet not feeding from that first kill. Instead, they would hunt down the remaining family members as the cries of their wounded rang in their ears. Their adrenal response of fight or flight, coupled with intense regret that they were leaving a loved one behind, imbued their blood with an effervescent fizz, making it lighter and more aromatic. The process of collecting such blood, however, was very wasteful. When the Myrmel were absorbed into House Drakan, I decreed that the process only be used for special celebrations, with the primary victim's blood used to feed the lower-born vyres.

author: Lowerniel Drakan
quote: The Pyrah were a loathsome tribe of carrion-eaters, and their ways had no place in a modern vampyric society. They would capture whole families of creatures at a time, keeping them in appalling conditions until death took the weakest of them. Any survivors would be mournful of such losses, their grief heightened by being left with the corpses of their families in tight confines. Once entire families had died off, the Pyrah would harvest their congealed blood for later consumption. The Pyrah had vast stores of this solidified blood and I'll admit that, out of curiosity, I did sample it. The smell was foul, the texture was greasy and the thought of ingesting it sickened me. The taste, however, was surprisingly complex and rich. Nevertheless, the practice was abhorrent, and thus I had the entire blood stores of the Pyrah destroyed, and the tribe alongside it.

author: Lowerniel Drakan
quote: Ah, the Shadum. Their main source of food was from a race of creatures they had enslaved, a subjugation these creatures had willingly entered into, submitting to another so they would not have to make choices on their own. Perhaps they held a symbiotic need to attach themselves to our kind for survival. Regardless, the Shadum were sadistic in their dealings with these beings, breeding them as both subservients and food. The blood of these creatures held a quality both salty and sweet - an intriguing combination, though not to my ideal tastes.

author: Lowerniel Drakan
quote: The Vitur were in thrall to their long-dead founder, whom they considered a 'god'. He was a figure of awe and wonder to the Vitur, and there were volumes of histories dedicated to him. Indeed, he was not only worshipped by his vyres, but a number of sapient races sacrificed themselves willingly out of respect for him and House Vitur's opulent culture. These creatures are now scarce on Vampyrium, but I was able to obtain a store of their blood. It holds an incredibly fresh and pure taste - pleasant, if a little bland.

author: Kaleb (Havenhythe)
quote: This place absolutely reeks! It's a heavy aroma of rotten plants, bubbling mud and something else I can't quite identify (and I will likely be thankful I can't)...though it's probably just the bogolins who live here. My guide had informed me that, odd-looking as they were, these bogolins weren't unfriendly. In fact, they sound not too dissimilar from the small goblin tribe that live in Bandlesbury, albeit a bit stinkier, and these ones made homes in giant snail shells, of all things.

During the early years of Queen Ninbaradari's reign, however, a series of increasingly severe earthquakes struck the island. The tremors continued for months before culminating in a single catastrophic event.

Certain sections appeared unnaturally smooth, as though bored through the land rather than formed by nature. As the expedition descended deeper, they discovered what appeared to be a vast cliffface of ivory-coloured stone. Then the cliff moved.
A sizeable wound penetrated its body, but yet the creature appeared to be healing. Though the creature seemed near death, it lived on.
From the exposed flesh flowed a thick white fluid that emitted a faint glow.
Through blood magic and divine experimentation, the millipede was prevented from dying. Bound to the mortal plane and incapable of escape, it became a permanent source of divine ichor.
Divine ichor was collected in vast quantities. The substance fuelled experiments, strengthened Queen Ninbaradari's followers and became the foundation upon which much of her growing power was built.
As the years passed, portions of the harvested ichor began to harden into an unfamiliar pale stone. Attempts to reverse the process proved futile.
By the time of Queen Ninbaradari's departure, much of its body had become petrified.

Whether it has finally died, or whether some fragment of life yet endures beneath its petrified shell, remains uncertain. The only thing known for certain is that the harvest never truly ended, as the creature is still harvested today, albeit for an entirely different purpose: now, for its stone.

author: Ninkurax
quote: The other lords did turn their backs upon the Lord of Fate. They built their temple up on high, left me trapped here to wait.

author: Ninkurax
quote: Yet all I did was to reveal how each of them would end. I did it as a way to warn; I would for any friend.

author: Ninkurax
quote: So down here in the dark I'm left, with skilled arachnomancy. I'll spin my webs and teach my kind to weave prophetic fancy. I leave behind the Book of Lies, so my children aren't alone.

author: Ninkurax
quote: Also a lantern of eight eyes; my body turned to stone.

When the scales of life and death formed the underworld it was but a void, lifeless and devoid of any semblance of our world. Magic flowed unlike the realm of the living, manifesting in four prime elements: Bone, Flesh, Spirit, and Miasma. It was with this magic that the so-called god of balance brought shape to the underworld. With shape came the dead, ferried by the god's chosen vassal. The god, lost in their compassion for the living, failed to foresee that their actions would disturb the flow of true death and the oblivion of the underworld. The elements, once silent, began to gather and pool, disrupted by the young god's actions. Slowly, they twisted, weaved, and grew stronger. It was here that the prime elementals of death were formed. In their antithesis of death, death gave birth to life.

The Lord of Bones was the next to take shape, an emptiness made manifest. It had no want or need, nothing more than a shell of potential. It ventured into the darkness, never to be seen again. The Noxious Miasma and Arisen Flesh were the last to form, twins born of the same sorrowful tale. One wanted what...

The elements, once silent, began to gather and pool, disrupted by the young god's actions. Slowly, they twisted, weaved, and grew stronger. It was here that the prime elementals of death were formed. In their antithesis of death, death gave birth to life.

Born into pain and longing, it searched for another like itself but was met only with the emptiness of the underworld. Unable to bear the longing, it tore itself asunder. The beings longed no more, but with their actions, spirit flowed from within. Torn apart yet together, they were lost beneath the waves that escaped their form.
